KLEOS I – Glory That Outlives the Mission: Robots Left Behind

KLEOS I is an interactive educational storytelling website that brings attention to the remarkable legacy of NASA equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars. Through engaging digital storytelling, NASA imagery, interactive 3D models and mission-based exploration, we showcase three historic missions: Apollo 11's Lunar Module Eagle, Surveyor 3, and the Spirit and Opportunity Mars Exploration Rovers.

Our project addresses the challenge of making the history and scientific significance of space exploration more accessible, engaging and understandable, particularly to students and young people. Rather than presenting these machines as abandoned equipment, KLEOS I tells the stories of their missions, discoveries and lasting contributions to science.

By combining technology, education, history and immersive storytelling, we transform forgotten space hardware into powerful reminders of human curiosity, innovation and exploration. Our goal is to inspire the next generation to explore STEM and appreciate that even when a mission ends, its legacy lives on.
details:
KLEOS I – Glory That Outlives the Mission: Robots Left Behind

KLEOS I is an interactive educational storytelling website that explores the legacy of human exploration beyond Earth by showcasing NASA equipment and robotic systems left behind on the Moon and Mars. The project focuses on three major missions: Apollo 11 and its Lunar Module Eagle, Surveyor 3, and NASA's Spirit and Opportunity Mars Exploration Rovers.

The website transforms historical space exploration information into an engaging digital learning experience. Users can explore dedicated mission pages, discover the history and scientific contributions of each piece of equipment, view NASA photographs, interact with 3D models where available, and navigate through illustrated storytelling chapters.

Our project aims to address the limited public awareness of the scientific and historical significance of equipment left behind during space exploration missions. Rather than viewing these objects as abandoned machinery, KLEOS I presents them as important historical artifacts that represent human innovation, scientific discovery and the progress of space exploration.

We developed the platform using HTML, CSS and JavaScript to create a responsive, interactive and visually engaging website. We incorporated official NASA images, mission information and available 3D resources to ensure authenticity and improve the learning experience. External resources and technologies, including Google's Model Viewer, help bring selected spacecraft and robotic equipment to life through interactive 3D visualization.

What makes KLEOS I creative is its storytelling approach. Instead of presenting space exploration as a collection of technical facts, we tell the stories of the machines that completed their missions but remained on other celestial bodies. The platform connects science, history, technology and digital storytelling to make space exploration more relatable, particularly to students and young people interested in STEM.

Our team considered accessibility, educational value, historical accuracy, user experience, visual appeal and the availability of authentic NASA resources throughout development. We also focused on making navigation straightforward so that visitors can easily move between the different missions and explore the content independently.

Ultimately, KLEOS I seeks to inspire curiosity about space exploration, promote STEM education and preserve awareness of the remarkable technological achievements that continue to tell humanity's story, even long after their missions have ended.
